Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

SPECIFICATION FOR 
CRICKET STUMPS AND BAILS 

( First Revision ) 



1. Scope — Covers requirements pertaining to materials, shape and dimensions, workmanship and 
finish of stumps and bails used in the game of cricket. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 2. 

3. Materials — The timber used for the manufacture of stumps and bails shall be of two grades, 
namely. Grade 1 and Grade 2, listed below. The timber shall be properly selected, seasoned, straight- 
grained (slope of grain not to exceed 1 in 15) and absolutely free from knots, warping and other 
defects. The moisture content shall be between 10 to 14 percent: 

Botanical Name 

Fraxinus spp. 
Quercus spp. 
Zantiioxylum riietsa DC. 
Dysoxylum malabaricum Bedd, 

Moras spp. 

Ouqeinia oojeinensis Hochreut. 

Grewia telii folia Vahl. 

Celtis australis Linn. 

Polyalthia spp. 

Mitragyna parvifoiia Korth, 

Adina cordifolia Hook. f. 

l\Aorus laevigata Wall, 

4. Workmanship and Finish — Each stump and bail shall be straight one piece and shall not have 
any joints. The top and the conical end of the stump shall not be covered with a metallic cap. The 
groove for bail shall be neatly made. 

4.1 There shall be no tool marks on the surface of the stumps and the bails. The surfaces shall be 
finished smooth. The stumps shall be given a protective coat of good grade of clear or pale t^oloured 
transparent varnish or both. The varnished surface shall be smooth, uniform and hard and shall be 
free from bubbles and tackiness. The varnished surface shall not peel off. 



Grade 


Trade Name 


1 


Ash 




Indian oak 




Mullilam 




White cedar

5, Test — Support the stump at its two ends with its axis horizontal. 

from its middle point suitably. Lift the weight through TOO mm and drop. 

times. The stump shall not show failure or damage at the end of the test 



Suspend a weight of 20 kg 
This shall be done 5 



6. Marking — Each stump shall be embossed with the name, initials or recognized trade-mark of the 
manufacturer on the conical end. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — The stumps ^nd bails shall be suitably packed as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

On the suggestion of Consultative Committee of Parliament for Department of Sports, the con- 
cerned Panel of Sports Goods Sectional Committee has brought in line this standard with the require- 
ments covered in respective Sports Goods Federation's Handbook.
